name: Ramon Laguarta

career.title: Several international roles in Europe and the U.S.
General manager roles (Greece Snacks; Iberia Snacks & Juices), Commercial VP for Europe, President of Eastern Europe Region
President (oversaw global category groups, global operations, corporate strategy, public policy)

background_rationale: Began in international roles at confectioner Chupa Chups and spent two decades running commercial and regional consumer-goods businesses across PepsiCo Europe before becoming president and CEO.

notable.summary: Completed PepsiCo's acquisition of SodaStream, announced in August 2018, as part of a push toward healthier products and less packaging waste.
Agreed to acquire Rockstar Energy for about $3.85 billion, expanding PepsiCo's energy-drink portfolio.
Announced the acquisition of prebiotic soda brand Poppi for more than $1.6 billion, following the $1.2 billion Siete Foods deal completed in January 2025.

In an agreement with activist investor Elliott Management, PepsiCo said it would cut nearly 20% of its U.S. product lineup by early 2026, close three manufacturing plants and reduce staff to focus on core brands.

personal_story.hook: A Barcelona native who started out at lollipop maker Chupa Chups now runs PepsiCo.
personal_story.summary: Laguarta is from Barcelona and studied business at ESADE before earning a master's in international management at Thunderbird in Arizona in 1986. He began his career at Spanish confectioner Chupa Chups, holding international roles in Europe and the U.S., then joined PepsiCo in 1996. Over two decades he ran snack and juice businesses in Greece and Iberia, led Eastern Europe, and became CEO of PepsiCo's Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa unit in 2014. Promoted to president in 2017, he moved to the U.S. and succeeded Indra Nooyi as CEO in October 2018, the company's sixth.
